newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Beer and textiles boost Abidjan Bourse.
newsitem.headline: Beer and textiles boost Abidjan Bourse.

text.p: Ivory Coast's Stock Exchange rose in the week to Friday, with textile manufacturer UNIWAX rising 3,230 to 69,820 and brewer SOLIBRA up 3,420 to 69,710, leading the way, its market report showed.
The All-Share BVA index rose 2.1 percent to 410.86, taking the 1997 rise to 14.83 percent. The 12 VB blue-chip index rose 2.77 percent 278.97 points, 15.28 percent up on the year.
The other main riser was tobacco company SITAB, up 2,500 to 42,000. The main loser, sack maker FILTISAC, was down 3,500 to 45,200.
A total of 7,748 shares worth of 182,691,870 CFA francs changed hands against 1,693 shares worth 41,493,560 CFA the previous week.

One trader explained the growing interest in the bourse by saying that, with board meetings imminent, investors were hoping for good news on dividends. Others said Ivorians were showing greater interest in the market, which has been heavily promoted as part of the government's privatisation efforts.
"It is more and more profitable to have shares than having money in banks, where interest rates are less than four percent," one told Reuters.
